message.content: Lions mate during the breeding season (typically late winter to early spring). A male will approach a receptive female, often after a scent-marking display. If she accepts, they engage in a brief courtship ritual involving vocalizations and body contact. The actual copulation lasts only a few minutes, but males may guard females for weeks afterward to ensure paternity. Females usually give birth to litters of 1–4 cubs after a gestation period of about 110 days.
